column1: # bloodtype_markers.tsv: the positions step 41 (scripts/41-bloodtype.sh, the BLOODTYPE
# processes) reads, GRCh38 (NCBI no-ALT analysis set), as a BED with extra columns: start is
# 0-based, end 1-based, so samtools bedcov reads this file as it is (comment and header lines removed).
# kind site: one variant that defines a blood group antigen. ref and alt are the VCF alleles
#   (left-aligned, + strand); ref_means and alt_means are what each allele gives. The variants
#   and their antigens are the ones the ISBT allele tables define, as packaged by RBCeq2 2.4.4
#   (database v2.5.1, MIT licence, Australian Red Cross Lifeblood; PyPI sdist sha256
#   was checked against Ensembl GRCh38 and its dbSNP id. The HPA rows come from dbSNP through
#   Ensembl GRCh38: that RBCeq2 database lists the HPA variants at their GRCh37 positions.
#   The neutrophil antigens (HNA-1, -3, -4, -5) are not in RBCeq2: their variants are the
#   ISBT HNA allele table's (Flesch et al. 2016, doi:10.1111/trf.13575), each mapped to
#   GRCh38 through Ensembl VEP on the gene's transcript, which also checked the REF base
#   (2026-10-25). dbSNP places some FCGR3B ids on FCGR3A, its near copy: the positions here
#   are FCGR3B's (exon 3, minus strand, so ref and alt are the complement of the c. bases).
#   The null rows (alt_means null) are the single-variant null alleles RBCeq2 2.4.4 lists for
#   SMIM1 (Vel), ABCB6 (Lan), ABCG2 (Jra), FUT1 (H), FUT2 (secretor), KEL (K0) and SLC14A1
#   (Jk(a-b-)): an allele that makes no antigen. Left out: alleles of two or more variants, the
#   deletions over 50 bp (JK*01N.01, ABCG2*01N.27), and KEL*02N.58, whose position KEL*02N.23
#   holds with another REF. Null alleles at one position with one REF share a row: alt is then
#   a comma list, and any of them is a null copy. The HPA-7 to -35 rows (HPA-15 aside) are
#   RBCeq2's HPA alleles; that database lists them at GRCh37 positions, so each was mapped to
#   GRCh38 with Ensembl's assembly map (2026-11-03). Every null and HPA-7 to -35 row was checked
#   on GRCh38 the same day: Ensembl VEP on the row's REF and ALT gave the allele's c. change on
#   its RefSeq transcript, and the REF is Ensembl's GRCh38 sequence. Where RBCeq2's text has a
#   slip, the c. change here is VEP's: HPA-13 is ITGA2 c.2483C>T, HPA-16 ITGB3 c.497C>T and
#   HPA-35 ITGB3 c.1514G>A. rsid is the dbSNP id Ensembl places at the row with the same change,
#   left empty when there is none.
# high_prevalence: the antigen of the row most people carry, so lacking it is rare (ISBT's
#   high-prevalence antigens Vel, Lan, Jra, H, k, Kpb, Jsb, Ku, Jk3, Lub, Dib, Coa; for platelets
#   HPA-1a and the a antigen of HPA-4 and HPA-6 to -35 but -15, whose b antigen is a
#   low-prevalence one). Step 41 lists first the systems where the genome predicts the person
# null_on: for a null row of a system with two-allele sites (Kell, Kidd), the antigens the null
#   allele is found with in the ISBT allele table, first choice first. Phase is not read, so a
#   null copy is placed on a chromosome that carries them.
# The RhD depth regions (the RHD gene, its ten exons and two flanks outside the common RHD
#   deletion) are the RHD row of bin/cn_loci.tsv; step 41 adds them to this table's sites for bedcov.
# caveat: why a short-read call at that site is less certain (confidence low in the table).
# meaning: for the platelet and neutrophil antigens, what lacking one of them means, written
#   into the note of the system's row when the genome predicts the person lacks it. It is
#   information about the antigen, not advice.
